direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: She glances at Hollis. Hollis glances at the door.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis sits down at the break-room table. Juno follows him in and settles at his feet. The lights, at long last, stop flickering.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: The vending machine makes a noise. It is not a good noise. It is not a bad noise. It is a noise like a thought.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: A cat slowly walks into the break room.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis stares at it. Juno stares at Hollis.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: One glowing mint drops into the tray.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: There is nothing specific you need right now. Try talking to people again, or moving to a new location.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: (Other open objectives:
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: . Press T for the to-do list.)
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: A large orange cat, sitting like a sergeant, with a slightly chewed sheet of paper stuck to the fur of his side like a medal. He looks at Hollis with authority and, faintly, hunger.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: SCANNER
spoken_text: CAT — SGT. BISCUIT. Rank: colony leader. Attached document: MANIFEST T-4417, PAGE 2 OF 2. Status: "worn as a medal". Weakness: fish crackers (80%).
direction: Dry handheld-device system voice; crisp, synthetic, mildly judgmental.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: The paper is loosened by a neat sweep of a paw. It slides off his fur and lands at Hollis's feet.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis offers the fish crackers. Sergeant Biscuit sniffs. He considers. He eats one with the dignity of a sommelier.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: PRUDENCE
spoken_text: Oh, don't. I'm not technically in possession of that.
direction: Sharp, defiant, comfortable where she should not be; amused by rules she no longer follows.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: The trail is already down.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis lays a line of kibble along the main aisle, from the racks toward the outbound dock. It's like leaving breadcrumbs, except for two hundred hungry witnesses.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis slits the stretched wrap. A small waterfall of brown pellets pours out. It smells like fish, tuna, and the entire history of feline temptation. This is not a counterweight.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis has enough kibble. Nobody needs a buffet.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: The shrink wrap is committed. Whatever is inside, the pallet is not going to volunteer it.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis grabs the vending machine and pulls. It tilts. It considers. It commits.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis climbs aboard. The forklift starts. Hollis backs up, turns, and puts a fork through a rack of tires. From a great distance, a small voice says "HR to the floor."
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis looks at the forklift. The keys are in it. Nobody is watching.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: TUCKER
spoken_text: Oh thank goodness! I thought I broke it! (beat) I did break it.
direction: Eager, enthusiastic, extremely willing to help; accidentally chaotic.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: The parts gate is locked. Hollis tries the old brass key. It fits like it was cut for a fired employee. Click. He's in.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: The parts gate is locked. A sign reads "PARTS: AUTHORIZED PERSONNEL ONLY". Someone with an old key would be very useful here.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Juno is not here. Hollis pets the air out of habit.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis pets Juno. Juno accepts this as her due.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis extends a hand toward a cat. The cat considers it, allows exactly two strokes, and then files a complaint with its eyes.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: There is no cat here. It is a strange thing to miss.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Feeding the cats is how this started. Nobody is going to say that out loud, but the narrator is thinking it.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis has never hit anything at work. It is why he is still employed. Mostly.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis considers it. HR, somewhere, sits up in its chair. He does not.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis is tempted. That is how the day started. He stays standing.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis does none of that. He is a professional. He is also very tall, and it would not end well near the racks.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis yells. The warehouse, which has heard everything, has no response. A cat blinks.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis does not smoke. That is Torvald's department, and Torvald would like it to stay that way.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis does not have any coffee. The break room pot smells like a rumor.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: It is the last decent coffee. It is not Hollis's. It has a destination.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis does not have a mint. Yet.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis holds the mint at arm's length. Not yet. Not until it is a real problem.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Nothing happens. Wrong game. (The vending machine hums, judgmentally.)
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis: tall, skinny, cap, gray shirt, blue vest, boots, stubble. He looks like a man who has already seen the incident report.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: The game saves itself as you go. (F5 also saves.) The warehouse does not.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis considers quitting. He has considered it since 2019. He is still here.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis swears mildly. A cat looks away, out of courtesy.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis waits. The clock in the break room agrees it is 9:02.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: . (The panel at the bottom shows them, too.)
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis checks his pockets:
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis considers that command. The parser considers Hollis. Neither is moved.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: That is not something Hollis knows how to do. He has tried "use", "look" and "scan"; these are his three verbs of choice.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis looks for a way to go there. He does not find one.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis doesn't see that here.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Using a forklift on that is technically a workplace incident. Hollis declines.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis doesn't have that.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis is back where he left off.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: This is Building 9 of the Gantry-Voss Logistics distribution center. Hollis is the shift lead here: he scans freight in, scans freight out, and is blamed in both directions.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: The fluorescent lights buzz at a frequency Hollis associates with mistakes.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Hollis wakes up at a break-room table. He does not remember falling asleep.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: The clock on the wall says 9:02. The clock has said 9:02 for as long as anyone can remember, so this is not information.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: His radio is missing. His handheld scanner (the thing that tells the warehouse computer where every pallet is) is dead. Someone has taken the last decent coffee. There is a crumpled shipping label stuck to his boot.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: On top of the vending machine, a cat sits looking at him. Nobody acknowledges this. Nobody is here. This is a warehouse. There are not supposed to be cats.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Through the door, faintly, reverse beepers and alarms. Somewhere, a forklift has an opinion.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: HOLLIS
spoken_text: Yeah. I know.
direction: Dry, tired, restrained; understated warehouse lead. Rarely matches the absurdity around him. Line direction: rubbing his face.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Today's job, such as it is: find out what everyone is so upset about, and get the scanner working so Hollis can check.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: It is a Tuesday. It is humid. It is going to get worse. (Controls: pick a verb, then click a thing. Right-click LOOKs. Enter types a command. Press H for a hint. Juno is your dog; the JUNO verb sends her to sniff or fetch.)
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.

speaker: NARRATOR
spoken_text: Juno trots over. She has the expression of a dog who tried to wake him twice and has decided to be gracious about it.
direction: Deadpan omniscient narrator; dry, observant, never sells the joke too hard.
